verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; no STOP (no UB, ABI regression or hidden obligation); four findings repaired (one failure-path compatibility divergence, one allocator release-coordinate set, two secret-residue classes).
scope: Per-file contract audit of provider KDF/DH key management, the legacy provider and legacy MAC, the ML common codec helper, the three ML-DSA signature rows, the ML-KEM codecs and the ML-KEM KEM rows. src/evp/method_store.rs and src/provider/init.rs were inspected and deferred as trust boundaries; the next two ordinary queue entries (ml_kem_codecs, ml_kem_kem) were audited in their place so the batch still covers eight files.

defects.description: dh_gen_common_set_params tested the named group's UID before storing it, so a rejected group left the previously selected group_nid; the authority assigns the UID first and therefore leaves NID_undef on the failure path.
defects.repair: Assign group_nid before testing it, matching dh_kmgmt.c:555-562. Successful-path behaviour is unchanged.

defects.description: The four OwnedBufs recorded the allocation line as their release line; the authority releases the i2d_pubkey failure block at :427, the i2d_prvkey failure block at :554, pubenc at :616 and prvenc at :617.
defects.repair: Use OwnedBuf::new_plain_released / new_cleansed_released with the authority's allocation and release coordinate pairs. Allocation coordinates and sizes are unchanged.

defects.description: The key_to_text stack copy of the private seed was never cleared, and the private-key DER buffers (prvenc and the i2d_prvkey output on failure) were released plainly, leaving seed/DK bytes in freed or reused storage.
defects.repair: Cleanse the to-text seed at function exit and give both private DER buffers a cleansing release while the unit still owns them. On success i2d_prvkey hands the block to the caller exactly as the authority does. Deliberate safety improvement over ml_kem_codecs.c.

defects.description: freectx cleansed only test_entropy_len bytes, and a refused or wrong-length test-entropy set resets that length to 0 after writing into the buffer, leaving earlier entropy bytes uncleansed.
defects.repair: freectx cleanses the whole test_entropy array, and each set-entropy attempt clears the array before copying and on every refusal. Deliberate deviation from ml_dsa_sig.c:79/420-427; not observable through the API.

retained_obligations.mechanism: C dispatch contexts and borrowed keys in keymgmt, mac_legacy_sig, ml_dsa_sig and ml_kem_kem
retained_obligations.obligation: Each unsafe entry point documents the corresponding OSSL_FUNC_KEYMGMT_*/SIGNATURE_*/KEM_* dispatch contract: a non-NULL live context from newctx/init and, where read, a live key owned by EVP_PKEY. The authority dereferences identically; no safe-Rust caller can reach these functions.
retained_obligations.status: documented dispatch precondition, not a hidden obligation

retained_obligations.obligation: The packet is a MaybeUninit<Wpacket> passed through WPACKET_init_der with a fresh 256-byte aid_buf. The init's NULL/zero refusal cannot occur at this call site, so WPACKET_cleanup always sees an initialised packet. The same shape is carried by the already-audited DSA/SLH-DSA signature units.
retained_obligations.status: statically established precondition; cleanup reachable only after successful init

retained_obligations.mechanism: ProvMlKemCtx::entropy pointer and ML-KEM/ML-DSA format-table consistency
retained_obligations.obligation: entropy is NULL or entropy_buf, so freectx/set_ctx_params/encapsulate cleanse a 32-byte in-context buffer only. The PKCS#8 table entries' offsets and lengths are consistent with p8_bytes and the variant key sizes, which is the bound the decode/encode walk relies on.

retained_obligations.mechanism: ML-KEM one-shot entropy on the ctext == NULL size query
retained_obligations.obligation: The size-query arm returns without cleansing so a caller that queries sizes and then encapsulates without re-init reuses the ikmE, exactly as ml_kem_kem.c:168-176 does. This is a deliberate compatibility behaviour, not an oversight; the buffer is cleansed on the next encapsulate and at teardown.

allocator_coordinate_changes.change: failure/teardown release coordinates now match the authority (:427, :554, :616, :617); allocation coordinates (:421, :486, :586, :602) and sizes are unchanged

OB-2 OwnedStr for provider names and search paths
OB-3 OwnedCtx/RawCtx/CtxDestroy and the block-vs-member destructor split for KdfData, DhGenCtx, ProvMlKemCtx and the legacy digest contexts, including the all-zero-block obligation
OB-4 member-buffer slots for seed/mdname/mdprops/sig fields replaced in place
RC-1 reference-count ownership for KdfData, MacKey and EVP_MD_CTX duplicate/free pairs
B19 BIGNUM/key cleansing through the primitive ML-DSA/ML-KEM/DH destructors
per-path allocator-coordinate contract established by M61/M62
OSSL_PARAM key-terminated array, locate and get_octet_string descriptor contracts
C ABI dispatch contracts for every extern "C" entry point, including caller-owned output buffers and NULL-or-live key arguments

secret_bearing_buffers.release: SECRET_DATA / CLEANSING_REQUIRED; full-array OPENSSL_cleanse in freectx and before every set-entropy copy and on every refusal; the earlier length-only cleansing was the M68-D4 residue
rand_tmp cleansed whenever it, not test_entropy, supplied the value; mu cleansed on every return of sign_msg_final and verify_msg_final
key is borrowed from EVP_PKEY (owned and cleansed there); context_string, sig and aid_buf are PUBLIC_DATA
SECRET_DATA allocated by CRYPTO_secure_malloc at :388 and adopted by ML_KEM_KEY; released by the key's secure-clear destructor on every success and failure path
copied by ossl_ml_kem_set_seed into key-owned cleansed storage; the DER input block belongs to PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO and is released by its own destructor
SECRET_DATA; OwnedBuf::new_cleansed_released cleanses it at :554 when encoding fails; on success the caller takes the block as the authority's OPENSSL_malloc contract requires
stack seed cleansed at function exit; prvenc uses a cleansing release at :617; pubenc is PUBLIC_DATA and uses plain release at :616
SECRET_DATA; cleansed after every encapsulation and in CtxDestroy::destroy_body; deliberately retained on the ctext == NULL size-query path, matching ml_kem_kem.c
seed cleansed through OwnedBuf::adopt_cleansed on replacement and CtxDestroy; mdname/mdprops are PUBLIC_DATA and use plain release
the chaining state is the context block itself; CRYPTO_clear_free over size_of::<T>() on every freectx/dup error path
propq is PUBLIC_DATA (property query) and freed plainly at the authority's per-path lines; the key reference and EVP_MAC_CTX are released through their refcount/free contracts

residuals: src/evp/method_store.rs and src/provider/init.rs remain the deferred registry and provider-initialisation boundaries at the head of the queue.
ML-KEM's ctext == NULL size-query path deliberately retains the one-shot ikmE entropy for the next call, matching the authority.
A private-key DER block handed to a caller by ossl_ml_kem_i2d_prvkey is caller-owned and released plainly by the authority's contract; the unit cleanses only blocks it still owns.
The legacy provider keeps a child library context alive across teardown, the documented default/base-provider shape rather than legacyprov.c's own OSSL_LIB_CTX_free.
No constant-time claim is made for ML-DSA, ML-KEM or the legacy units from source inspection.
